commands.review_summary:
The branch replaces brace-count JSON block consumption in status-all Gateway log summaries with a quote/escape-aware scanner and adds a regression test for OAuth messages containing braces.

PR surface: Source +21, Tests +13. Total +34 across 2 files.

Reproducibility: yes. from source inspection: current main counts every closing brace in `consumeJsonBlock`, so the supplied valid JSON fragment with a quoted `}` can truncate the parsed block. I did not run a live current-main `status --all` command.

target.title: fix: keep status OAuth diagnostics when messages contain braces
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running `openclaw status --all` could see incomplete OAuth refresh diagnostics when a provider error message contained a brace character.

The affected surface is the read-only `status --all` Gateway log summary. When the Gateway log tail included a token-refresh JSON block like this:

```text
[openai] Token refresh failed: 401 {
"error":{"code":"invalid_grant","message":"Session invalidated } due to signing in again"}
}
```

the summarizer counted the `}` inside the quoted message as the end of the JSON block. That made `JSON.parse` receive an incomplete object, so the summary lost the useful provider reason and re-auth hint.

Before this patch, the status report could render:

```text
[openai] token refresh 401
```

The expected diagnostic is:

```text
[openai] token refresh 401 invalid_grant · re-auth required
```

## Why This Change Was Made

The log summarizer now scans Gateway JSON fragments with string and escape awareness before deciding where the JSON block ends. Braces inside quoted JSON strings no longer affect block depth, while real structural `{` / `}` characters still determine the end of the block.

This keeps the existing compact OAuth diagnostic behavior and only fixes the parser boundary. It does not change Gateway runtime behavior, authentication behavior, or the log format.

## User Impact

Operators get clearer `openclaw status --all` output when OAuth refresh fails. Provider messages containing `{` or `}` no longer hide reason codes such as `invalid_grant` or targeted guidance such as `re-auth required`.

This is especially useful during login/session-expiry troubleshooting, where the missing reason code is the difference between a generic status line and an actionable re-auth hint.

## Real Behavior Proof

- **Behavior addressed:** `summarizeLogTail` could truncate a token-refresh JSON block when a quoted provider message contained `}`.
- **Affected workflow:** `openclaw status --all` reads Gateway log tails in `status-all` diagnosis and summarizes OAuth refresh failures for operator diagnostics.
- **Root cause:** the old block reader counted `{` and `}` with plain string splitting, so it could not distinguish structural braces from braces inside JSON strings.
- **Fix:** replace the plain brace counter with a small scanner that tracks quoted strings and escaped characters.

Before/after example:

| Input condition | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OAuth JSON message contains `}` | `[openai] token refresh 401` | `[openai] token refresh 401 invalid_grant · re-auth required` |
| OAuth JSON message has no embedded braces | unchanged | unchanged |
| Long OAuth message with UTF-16 characters | unchanged truncation behavior | unchanged truncation behavior |

## Evidence

### Exact Reproduction

The broken input is a valid Gateway OAuth refresh log fragment where the provider message contains a brace:

```text
[openai] Token refresh failed: 401 {
"error":{"code":"invalid_grant","message":"Session invalidated } due to signing in again"}
}
```

Before this patch, `summarizeLogTail` counted the quoted `}` as structural JSON and produced only:

```text
[openai] token refresh 401
```

After this patch, the same input keeps the provider code and action hint:

```text
[openai] token refresh 401 invalid_grant · re-auth required
```

### Commands Run

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/status-all/gateway.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       4 passed (4)
```

```text
$ git diff --check -- src/commands/status-all/gateway.ts src/commands/status-all/gateway.test.ts
EXIT=0
```

Regression coverage added:

- `keeps OAuth JSON diagnostics when the message contains braces`
- Verifies that a message containing `}` still summarizes to `invalid_grant · re-auth required`.

Existing coverage retained:

- permanent OAuth refresh failures are classified as `re-auth required`
- long OAuth diagnostics remain UTF-16 safe when truncated
- large log-tail reads still return complete recent lines

Remote Testbox proof was not available in this checkout because:

```text
$ node scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs warmup --provider blacksmith-testbox --keep --timing-json
[crabbox] selected binary failed basic --version/--help sanity checks
```

What was not tested:

- Live `openclaw status --all` against a real Gateway log file containing this exact provider message. The behavior is covered at the summarizer boundary used by `status-all` diagnosis.

## Risk Checklist

- **User-visible behavior:** Yes, but limited to clearer `openclaw status --all` diagnostic text.
- **Runtime/auth behavior:** No. The change only affects log-tail summarization.
- **Config/env/migration behavior:** No.
- **Security/secrets behavior:** No. Existing downstream redaction in the status-all diagnosis path is unchanged.
- **Plugin/provider/channel SDK behavior:** No.
- **Highest-risk area:** Low. The parser only changes how a bounded diagnostic JSON block is grouped before `JSON.parse`.
- **Mitigation:** Focused regression test covers the failure trigger; existing status-all gateway tests still cover the normal OAuth and UTF-16 truncation paths.

Closes: N/A
